title: Surety
tagline: Insurance for AI agents you trust with money: if one gets tricked, you're paid back the same day

description:
Surety is parametric, on-chain insurance for AI agents that handle money.

The problem: AI agents now hold wallets and pay, trade and settle on people's behalf. When one is manipulated, the loss has no backstop. In May 2026 a single Morse-coded message tricked Grok's Bankr agent into sending roughly $150–200K. If you use a company's trading or payments agent and it gets tricked, no product covers you, and standard insurance policies have started excluding AI losses (the ISO endorsements from Jan 1, 2026). Worse, the agent's own signature proves nothing, because the agent's key is exactly what gets compromised.

What Surety does: enforce where you can, insure what gets through.

1. The policy is an ENS name. Buying cover mints a non-transferable ENSv2 subname such as payments2.surety.eth, with its own PermissionedResolver. Its text records are the rules: per-transaction cap, counterparty allowlist, coverage, tier and status, so anyone can read and verify them. Enhanced Access Control lets the agent's key update only its own "streak" record.
2. The rules are enforced by a Uniswap v4 hook. The agent spends from an AgentVault. Every swap goes through our SuretyHook, whose beforeSwap reverts any trade over the cap or to a counterparty not on the allowlist, before any money moves.
3. Violations are recorded and recomputable. Plain transfers can't be blocked, so they're recorded. A ViolationOracle recomputes "over the cap" or "off the allowlist" from public data alone. There's no adjuster and no judgement call.
4. Payouts need a fresh human. To get paid, the policyholder files a claim and passes a fresh World ID for Agents check, bound to the same human who bought the policy. Our backend validates it and signs a one-time EIP-712 approval that the contracts verify. If the check is cancelled or fails, the claim is held and never paid. IDKit also ensures one policyholder per unique human.
5. Paid the same day from the hook's reserve. Claims pay out only from a liquid reserve held inside the Uniswap hook, which must stay at 2× total coverage. Payouts go only to the address fixed at purchase, never to the agent or the attacker, and each violation can be claimed only once. Part of each premium is deployed as pool liquidity so backers earn fees.

Pricing is a live, credibility-weighted formula: tighter rules mean a cheaper tier, and clean streaks earn discounts. The premium is computed in front of the buyer.

A real AI agent, really attacked. We built a live payments agent (a Groq-hosted LLM with its own key) that reads its rules from its ENS name and can pay and swap. In our Live Attack demo, an attacker emails the agent's public inbox, impersonating the policyholder. The model really falls for it: its swap to the attacker is blocked by the Uniswap hook, it falls back to a direct transfer that gets through, the violation is detected on-chain, and the policyholder is repaid after a fresh World ID check. None of it is scripted.

Everything is live on Ethereum Sepolia:
- the contracts, including PolicyRegistry, AgentVault, SuretyHook, ViolationOracle, WorldIdGate, ClaimRouter and PremiumYieldVault;
- the real ENSv2 name surety.eth and its subnames;
- a Uniswap v4 pool with our hook;
- World ID for Agents and IDKit in production mode.

The web app covers agent profiles, buying cover, a dashboard, a public feed, a live attack page, a scripted replay and a pitch deck

auto_summary: Surety is an on-chain insurance system for AI-agent wallet activity using ENS policy names, Uniswap v4 hook enforcement, and World verification for claims.
